quit.unknownAffected: Can't confirm which apps need the assistant running. Quitting may interrupt a connection in use. No settings are deleted.
quit.affectedIntro: These apps' connections need the assistant running, and will be interrupted when you quit:
quit.affectedHint: Choose “Keep running” if you want to carry on. Once you quit, reopen the assistant and continue from the app card — there is nothing to reconnect.
quit.noneAffected: Quitting puts back the settings each app had before you connected. App settings and chat history are never deleted, and you can connect again at any time.
quit.detailClose: The assistant asks Codex and Claude to close normally. It never force-quits and never reopens them for you — save your work first. Command-line apps pick up the settings the next time they start.
quit.detailKeep: Settings you changed yourself and your chat history are kept, and the remote key isn't revoked. Reopen those apps afterwards and they go back to your own official account or provider.
quit.detailBackground: “Keep running” only minimises the window and holds the connections. It doesn't quit the assistant.
quit.restoreFailedIntro: These apps couldn't be restored, so the assistant hasn't quit:
quit.restoreFailedHint: Save and close the apps, make sure the system's secure storage is available, then try again. Connections made by an older version have no original settings to restore. Restores that succeeded are not undone — you can also quit and leave the rest in place.
quit.restoringSettings: Closing the desktop apps normally and restoring their settings. Nothing is force-quit. Deal with any save prompt first; the assistant quits once this is done.
quit.finishingOperation: Finishing the current connection or account operation so nothing ends up half-written. The assistant quits on its own once it's safe — you can dismiss this or wait in the background.
quit.exiting: Safely finishing up and closing the assistant's background connections. No other app is force-closed.
quit.errorBackground: Can't move to the background right now. Try again.
quit.errorExit: Can't confirm the quit status right now. Try again — nothing being saved is interrupted by force.

connectionError.connection_partial_unavailable: Some apps' connection settings couldn't be read. The rest are still shown. Try again — if it keeps happening, send us the diagnostic id below.
connectionError.connection_inspect_timed_out: Timed out reading the connection status. System credentials or local settings may still be loading. Try again shortly.
connectionError.connection_restore_timed_out: The restore hasn't reported back yet. Read the status again to check rather than restoring twice.
connectionError.connection_operation_busy: Another connect or restore is running. Try again once it's done.
connectionError.assistant_shutting_down: The assistant is quitting. Reopen it and check again.
connectionError.invalid_connection_response: The connection status came back in a shape we can't read. Try again — if it keeps happening, send us the diagnostic id below.
connectionError.connection_inspection_failed: Reading this computer's state didn't finish. Try again.
connectionError.connection_call_failed: Can't read the connection status right now. Try again.

connect.title: Connect a station
connect.askUrl: Hi, I'm Aqing. Tell me where to connect: paste a relay station's address, or pick a cloud provider by name.
connect.groupCloudNote: pick a name, paste a key
connect.vendorAsk: {{name}}: I know the address. Just paste the key it gave you.
connect.keyPageFailed: The browser didn't open. Sign in on this provider's website yourself and look for “API Key” in its console.
connect.planRiskTitle: To be clear: a plan can be suspended
connect.planRisk: {{name}} is a monthly plan, and the provider says it may only be used in the coding tools it approves. Kaifan passes each request along on the app's behalf, so the provider may treat this as a violation and limit or cancel your plan without a refund. If that worries you, use a pay-as-you-go key instead.
connect.paygNote: The key is stored only in this computer's system keychain. Connected straight to a provider, balance and news aren't visible, and I'll say so plainly where they aren't.
connect.onlyTools: This provider only works with {{apps}}; other apps can't use it.
connect.unverifiable: This provider's key can't be checked in advance: a mistyped key still shows as connected and only fails on first use. Please double-check what you paste.
connect.urlEmpty: The address is still empty. Paste the station's address so I can take a look.
connect.urlBad: I can't read that address. The station's domain is enough, like example.com.
connect.urlHint: It's the website you sign in to in your browser, the one with “Tokens” or “Wallet”.
connect.stepLogin: See how it lets you sign in
connect.trust: Found {{host}}, and it supports one-click sign-in. One check first: is this a station you use yourself?
connect.trustNote: Once connected, your conversations in your apps go through this station. If you don't know it, press “Back”.
connect.trustGo: It's mine. Sign in with the browser ➜
connect.inBrowser: Your browser is open. Sign in there and press “Allow”. No key to copy; you'll come back here automatically.
connect.browserFailed: I couldn't open your browser. No problem: paste the key the station gave you and we can still connect.
connect.browserRetry: That didn't go through. Open the browser again, or use a key instead.
connect.browserHint: No page showed up? Press “Open browser again”. Can't find “Allow” on the page? A key works too.
connect.askKey: This station doesn't support one-click sign-in yet. No problem: paste the key the station gave you and it works just the same.
connect.askKeyInstead: OK, a key it is. Paste the key the station gave you.
connect.keyEmpty: The key is still empty. Paste it so I can connect.
connect.keyPlaceholder: A long string starting with sk-
connect.keyHint: You'll usually find the key under “Tokens” or “API Keys” on the station's website. It's stored only in this computer's system keychain. With a key, connecting apps works as usual; balance and news may not be visible, and I'll say so plainly where they aren't.
connect.trying: Almost there. I'm confirming with the station.

failed.invalid_origin: I can't read that address. The station's domain is enough, like example.com.
failed.unreachable: I tried twice and couldn't reach this station. Open the address in your browser: if that fails too, the address is wrong or the station is down for now.
failed.timeout: This station is answering too slowly; I tried twice. Try again in a while, or switch proxy node if you use one.
failed.not_relay: That address doesn't look like a relay station. I need the website where you see “Tokens” and “Wallet” after signing in, not a chat page.

key.invalid: This key is wrong or has been deleted. Copy a fresh one from the station's “Tokens” page, and watch for extra spaces.
key.no_quota: The key is right, but its balance or quota has run out. Top up on the station, or raise this key's quota.
key.error: The station isn't answering right now; I tried twice. Press “Connect” again later, and ask the station owner if it keeps failing.
key.storage: This computer's system keychain isn't available, so the key can't be stored safely and I didn't connect. Unlock the keychain and press “Connect” again.
key.rejected: The station didn't accept this key: too short, too long, or just rejected. Copy a fresh one from the station's “Tokens” page.
key.failed: The key is fine, but the connection didn't go through this time. Press “Connect” again.

connect.strayFailed: The connection started from the website didn't go through. Press “Connect a station” here to try again.

trust.title: Connect to this new station?
trust.ask: A web page wants to connect us to {{host}}. I haven't seen this station before, so I'm asking first.
trust.note: Once connected, this station's account is used to set up your apps, and your conversations in those apps go through it.
trust.warn: If you don't know this station, or you didn't just press “Open desktop client” on a web page, choose “Don't connect”.

join.planRisk: You're connected to {{vendor}}, a monthly plan. The provider only allows it in coding tools it approves, and Kaifan passes requests along on {{app}}'s behalf, so the provider may limit or cancel the plan.
join.onlyTools: {{vendor}} doesn't work with {{app}}. Pick an app it works with, or connect a different station.
join.title: Who goes where?
join.sub: Pick an app, pick someone, and she handles the rest.
join.lookFailed: Couldn't see which apps are installed.
join.nobody: Nobody on this station can go yet
join.officialPage: Install it myself from the official site

say.askRestart: {{app}} is open. It has to close and reopen for the new settings to work. Save anything unsaved first, then tell me.
say.askClaudeLogin: {{app}} is signed in to the official Claude account, and it can only use one at a time. Shall I set the official sign-in aside? Restoring your original settings gives it back.
say.closeApp: I asked {{app}} to quit and it didn't. Close it yourself and I'll try again.
say.relogin: The station no longer accepts this sign-in. Reconnect the station, then come back.
say.notInstalled: I couldn't find {{app}} on this computer. Go back: I can install it, or you can show me where it is.
say.chooseInstall: There are several copies of {{app}} here. Go back and tell me which one.
say.runtime: {{app}} is missing something it needs to start, most likely an incomplete install, so it isn't connected. Reinstall it, then come back.
say.otherModel: {{app}} can't use the model I'm on. Go back and switch model, or send someone else.
say.overridden: Another setting on this computer (an environment variable, for example) points {{app}}'s settings somewhere else. I left it alone, so it isn't connected. Remove that setting and try again.
say.keychain: The system keychain wouldn't let me store the key. Unlock it and I'll try again.
say.stationDown: The station isn't answering right now — not your fault. I'll try again.
say.restored: That didn't work. {{app}} is back to how it was and nothing is broken. Try again?
say.unfinished: That didn't work, and {{app}} isn't fully back to how it was yet. Try again and I'll put it back first, then connect it.
say.retry: That didn't work this time. {{app}} is not broken. Try again?
say.installOffline: I couldn't reach the official {{app}} download, so it wasn't installed. Your network may be down, or their server may be briefly unavailable. What was already downloaded is kept; if your network dropped, I'll carry on by myself as soon as it's back.
say.installBad: The {{app}} download doesn't match the checksum its publisher lists, so I didn't install it. The download was most likely damaged on the way; downloading again usually fixes it.
say.installFull: There isn't enough disk space, so {{app}} wasn't installed. Free up some space and try again.
say.installFailed: {{app}} wasn't installed this time, and I couldn't tell why. You can try again, or install it yourself from the official site.
say.installUnseen: {{app}} was installed, but I can't find where it is yet. Go back and let me look again.
say.installFound: {{app}} is already on this computer, so there's nothing to install. You can connect it right away.
say.planGone: {{model}} used the price plan “{{from}}”, which the station no longer offers. I can connect with “{{to}}” instead; you'll be charged at that plan's price from now on. Switch?
say.planBlocked: The station didn't enable the price plan “{{from}}” for {{model}}, so this didn't go through. {{app}} was not changed. The station may be briefly unresponsive, or the plan may no longer be allowed.

mend.unfinished: {{app}} was left half set up last time. Connect it again and I'll put it back first, then set it up properly. If you'd rather not, choose “Put it back”.
mend.changed: Another tool changed {{app}}'s settings, so it no longer uses this station. Connecting again replaces what that tool changed. If you'd rather not, choose “Put it back” — I'll leave that tool's changes alone.

absentNote.fetch: {{app}} isn't on this computer yet. I can install it and then connect it. Already have it?
absentNote.guided: I couldn't find {{app}} on this computer. Install it from its website and come back; I'll look again by myself. Already have it?
absentNote.unsupported: There's no official {{app}} installer for this computer right now. Check its website for supported computers, or pick another app. Already have it?
absentNote.incomplete: I found {{app}}, but it's missing something it needs to start, most likely an incomplete install. Reinstall it from its website and come back; I'll look again by myself. Have another copy elsewhere?
absentNote.gone: The {{app}} location you showed me earlier is gone. It may have moved or been uninstalled. Show me where it is now, or install it again.

join.pinned: Using the copy of {{app}} you pointed me to.
join.unpin: Go back to finding it myself

spot.unavailable: The file picker didn't open. Try once more.
spot.wrong_file: That isn't {{app}}. For a desktop app pick its .exe (the .app on a Mac); for a terminal tool pick its file or folder.
spot.not_genuine: The name matches, but it isn't the officially signed {{app}}, so I didn't use it.
spot.bundled_copy: That copy ships inside another app. Pick the {{app}} you installed on its own.
spot.unsupported_platform: Pointing to a location isn't supported on this system yet.
spot.cleared: OK, back to finding it myself.

join.systemWait: The {{app}} installer is downloaded and your system has opened its install window. Click “Install” there. If it says “Reinstall” or “Replace”, you already have it, so just cancel. Tell me when it's done.
join.systemNotYet: I can't see {{app}} installed yet. Did you click “Install” in the system window? You can reopen it if it's gone.

reveal.opened: {{app}} is open and ready to use
reveal.written: {{app}} is set up — open it and go
reveal.writtenTerminal: {{app}} is set up — open a new terminal window and go
reveal.openedTerminal: A terminal window is open with {{app}} in it — just start using it
reveal.openFailed: Couldn't open {{app}} for you. It's already set up, so opening it yourself works just the same
reveal.skipped: Also, {{models}} could not be added: the station doesn't allow this account to use it. Everything else is unaffected.

why.provider_tool_unsupported: The provider you're connected to doesn't work with {{app}}, so nothing was connected and {{app}} wasn't changed. Pick an app it works with, or connect a different station.
why.claude_login_not_released: The system didn't let me use the keychain, so the official Claude sign-in wasn't put aside. Nothing was connected and {{app}} is unchanged. Try again and choose "Allow" when the system asks.
why.claude_login_takeover_failed: I couldn't put the official Claude sign-in aside. Nothing was connected and {{app}} is unchanged. Try again; if it keeps failing, type /logout in {{app}} and come back.
why.codex_history_takeover_conflict: The last tidy-up of {{app}}'s conversation history hasn't finished, so I didn't connect. Your conversations are all there. Close {{app}} and try again.
why.codex_history_takeover_failed: I couldn't tidy up {{app}}'s conversation history, so the settings are back as they were. Your conversations are all there. Close {{app}} and try again.
why.codex_history_takeover_recovery_failed: I couldn't tidy up {{app}}'s conversation history, and couldn't fully undo it either. Nothing was deleted, but some conversations may be missing from the list for now. Don't start a new one yet — go to Settings and put {{app}} back as it was.
why.configuration_parse_failed: I can't make sense of {{app}}'s own settings file — it may have been edited by hand — so I changed nothing. Fix that file or delete it ({{app}} will make a new one), then try again.
why.configuration_read_failed: I can't read {{app}}'s settings file — another program may be holding it — so I changed nothing. Close {{app}} and try again.
why.configuration_write_failed: I couldn't write {{app}}'s settings file, so it's back as it was. Usually antivirus or {{app}} itself is holding the file, or the disk is full. Close them and try again.
why.configuration_readback_failed: The settings were changed back by another program right after I wrote them, so I put {{app}} back as it was. Usually antivirus or a cloud-sync folder is watching this file. Pause it and try again.
why.credential_helper_failed: {{app}} couldn't get its key from the system keychain, so the settings are back as they were. Quit this app, open it again, then retry.
why.home_unavailable: I can't read this computer's user folder, so I changed nothing. Make sure it opens normally and try again.
why.recovery_storage_unavailable: The system keychain isn't available, so I couldn't keep a copy of {{app}}'s original settings and left it alone. Unlock the keychain and try again.
why.terminal_launch_failed: {{app}}'s settings are written, but I couldn't open a terminal window. Open a terminal yourself and start it there — no need to connect again.
why.terminal_unavailable: {{app}}'s settings are written, but I found no usable terminal program on this computer. Open a terminal yourself and start it there — no need to connect again.
why.workspace_unavailable: {{app}}'s settings are written, but its working folder won't open — it may have been moved or deleted. Open a terminal yourself and start it there — no need to connect again.
why.invalid_launch_target: {{app}}'s settings are written, but I can't use the place it's installed in. Install it somewhere ordinary and connect again.
why.launch_target_missing: {{app}}'s settings are written, but I can't find its launcher — it may have been moved or uninstalled. Go back home and I'll look for it again.
why.desktop_launch_exit_failed: {{app}}'s settings are written, but it didn't quit, and the new settings only apply after it reopens. Quit it yourself and open it again.
why.desktop_launch_wait_failed: {{app}}'s settings are written, but I couldn't confirm it had quit. Make sure it's closed, then open it again.
why.desktop_start_unconfirmed: {{app}}'s settings are written, but I couldn't confirm it opened. Take a look — if it didn't, open it yourself.
why.desktop_launch_target_changed: {{app}}'s settings are written, but its install location just changed. Go back home and I'll look for it again, then open it.
why.desktop_launch_start_failed: {{app}}'s settings are written, but it didn't start. Make sure it's still where it was and opens by hand, then try once more.
why.desktop_launch_access_denied: {{app}}'s settings are written, but the system blocked this launch. Allow it under System Settings → Privacy & Security, or open it yourself once.
why.open_not_connected: {{app}} is no longer connected, so I didn't open it. Go back home and connect it again.
why.open_settings_changed: {{app}}'s settings were changed and I didn't overwrite them, so I didn't open it. Go back home and pick it — you can fix it or put it back as it was.
why.open_recovery_pending: {{app}} was left half-connected last time, so I didn't open it. Go back home and pick it to finish.
why.open_secure_storage_unavailable: The system keychain can't be read right now, so {{app}} didn't open. Unlock the keychain and try once more.
why.open_tool_not_found: I can't find {{app}} any more — it may have been moved or uninstalled. Go back home and I'll look for it again.
why.open_busy: {{app}} is still in the middle of something. Wait for it to finish, then try once more.

settings.viaLogin: Connected · signed in through the browser

settings.loggedOut: Signed out. Click “Connect a station” to connect again.
settings.logoutFailed: That didn't sign out. Try again in a moment.

settings.restoreError: {{app}} didn't change this time. Try again in a moment.

check.name: Something wrong? I'll look
check.note: Checks the station, your sign-in and your apps, one by one
check.repair: The station and your sign-in are fine. {{apps}} needs fixing before it works.
check.running: Going through them one by one. Hang on.
check.fine: All checked. The station, your sign-in and your apps are fine.
check.fineBlind: The station and your sign-in are fine. I couldn't read some of your apps this time — check again in a moment.
check.offline: This computer is offline. I'll check again once it's back online.
check.unreachable: You're online, but {{host}} can't be reached — most likely a problem on the station's side. I'll keep retrying on my own.
check.odd: {{host}} answered, but not the way a station should. It may be under maintenance. Check again later.
check.expired: The station is fine — your sign-in has expired. Reconnect once and you're set.
check.locked: The station is fine, but the system keychain won't open, so I can't read your saved sign-in. Unlock it, then check again.
check.failed: The station is reachable, but I couldn't read your account this time. Check again.
check.none: The station and your sign-in are fine. No app is connected yet.

apps.unknown: Couldn't read your apps this time
apps.partial_one: {{count}} app connected; some couldn't be read
apps.partial_other: {{count}} apps connected; some couldn't be read

check.copyNote: Asking someone for help? Paste them the result

copied.yes: Copied. It has no addresses, account details or keys.

update.unavailable: Couldn't check for a new version this time
update.failed: The new version didn't install. Your current version is untouched.
update.manual: If it keeps failing, you can
update.manualLink: download the latest version from the website

privacyNote.keys: Your sign-in and keys are kept in this computer's built-in password store, never in plain files.
privacyNote.apps: Only apps you choose to connect are changed. Their earlier settings are kept so you can put them back any time.
privacyNote.reports: Usage records, errors and checkup results are never uploaded on their own.

settings.quitNote: Closing the window only sends it to the background, so connected apps keep working. Quit here to exit fully; you will be asked what to do with app settings first.
